title: Modality-agnostic directed connectivity added to jnwb.connectivity: granger / phase_slope_index / transfer_entropy on one (X, Y) contract

claims.text: All three estimators accept the same signal container via as_trials(): 1-D (n_times,), 2-D (n_trials, n_times) with selectable time_axis, or a list of 1-D trials (ragged truncated to the shortest, logged). 3-D input is rejected rather than guessed at, and any non-finite sample is a hard ValueError -- connectivity never imputes. bin_spikes() bridges spike times into the same (n_trials, n_bins) array, so LFP / binned spikes / MUAe / band power all go through identical code with no modality-specific arguments.

Each estimator was validated against a system whose direction is true by construction, not against real data. GC on an AR system where x drives y at lag 2: x->y = 0.3876 (p < 1e-6), y->x = -0.0001 (p = 0.585). PSI on a 20 Hz source with y delayed 10 ms: psi = +0.1343, jackknife z = 3.04. TE on the same AR system: 0.1982 bits, surrogate p = 0.010, reverse direction p = 0.594. Independent white noise returns null for all three.
claims.receipt: scratchpad verify_directed.py 30/30 checks passed; same ground truths encoded as pytest cases (test_granger_recovers_known_direction, test_psi_sign_follows_the_leading_signal, test_transfer_entropy_recovers_known_direction, test_granger_null_on_independent_signals)

claims.text: The three methods were shown to fail and succeed in different places, which is the justification for carrying all three. (a) Quadratic coupling y[t] ~ x[t-1]^2: GC p = 0.220 (blind), TE p = 0.010 (detects). (b) Zero-lag common source (volume conduction / shared reference): PSI z = 0.59 vs z = 3.04 for the genuinely delayed pair. (c) Conditional GC on a common driver z: unconditional x->y = 1.5139 collapses to -0.0001 once z enters both models.

Determinism: every surrogate path is seeded (default seed=0) and repeat calls return bit-identical values. Multiplicity: directed_network() declares the FDR family as all N*(N-1) ordered pairs, not per-cell. Bias: raw TE is positively biased at finite n, so surrogates run by default (n_surrogates=200) and both raw and bias-corrected (effective) TE are reported; n_surrogates=0 emits an explicit warning rather than a clean-looking number. Undersampling: TE reports samples_per_joint_state and warns below 10. PSI refuses to fabricate a band it cannot resolve -- theta (4-8 Hz) at nperseg=256/fs=1000 (df = 3.91 Hz, 1 bin) returns NaN plus a warning instead of a number.

PSI must average cross- and auto-spectra over Welch segments pooled across trials. A single-segment coherency has magnitude exactly 1 by construction, so its phase-slope sum carries no coherence weighting and is not interpretable. The pre-existing jnwb.jrsa._phase_slope() takes a single rfft of the whole raveled record and has exactly this defect; the new phase_slope_index() segments (280 segments in the validation case) and additionally reports the Nolte jackknife standard deviation and z.
claims.receipt: jnwb/jrsa.py:1360-1378 (single np.fft.rfft on ravelled input, no segmenting); new implementation validated at n_seg=280 with z=3.04 on a known 10 ms delay

claims.text: The legacy granger_causality(signal1, signal2), spike_mutual_information(), and network_topology() signatures and return dicts are untouched. New names are additive: granger / phase_slope_index / transfer_entropy (aliases gc / psi / te), directed_connectivity, directed_network, as_trials, bin_spikes, DirectedResult, CANONICAL_BANDS. DirectedResult supports dict-style __getitem__/get so it reads like the older dict returns. jnwb.gc does not shadow the stdlib gc module for importers.
claims.receipt: python -c 'import jnwb; import gc as _gc; _gc.isenabled()' -> True, all new names present on the package

resolved_issues.was: Band-definition drift, NOT introduced here and NOT fixed here: jnwb/spectral.py:169-177 cross_area_coherence() still defaults to the pre-correction set (alpha 8-12, beta 12-30, low_gamma 30-55, high_gamma 55-90).
resolved_issues.resolution: Fixed on user instruction, in BOTH drift sites -- the audit had found only one. jnwb/spectral.py:cross_area_coherence and jnwb/factories.py:result_from_tfr_analysis now import CANONICAL_BANDS instead of hardcoding a dict. Documented as an intentional break at each change site with the blast radius spelled out: band NAMES are unchanged so callers keyed by name keep working, but the NUMBERS move (alpha 8-12 -> 8-14, beta 12-30 -> 14-30, low_gamma 30-55 -> 30-50, high_gamma 55-90 -> 50-80) and 'delta' is dropped because no project doctrine defines its edges. Passing freq_bands= explicitly still reproduces the old output. No production script called either with default bands.

resolved_issues.was: Spectral (Geweke) Granger causality is not implemented -- frequency-resolved GC needs Wilson spectral factorisation of the VAR.
resolved_issues.resolution: Implemented as granger_spectral() (alias sgc). The original framing was imprecise and is corrected: Wilson spectral factorisation is required only for the NON-parametric variant that starts from an observed cross-spectrum. The parametric route needs no factorisation -- fit the bivariate VAR once, form H(f) = A(f)^-1 and S(f) = H Sigma H^H, and apply Geweke's instantaneous-causality normalisation. Reports per-band means, peak frequency per direction, VAR spectral radius as a stationarity receipt, and optional surrogates.
resolved_issues.receipt: Geweke decomposition identity holds -- the frequency average equals the time-domain value to 2.0% (spectral 0.7878 vs time-domain 0.8036) on an AR system with a 20 Hz resonance; spectral GC peaks at exactly 20.0 Hz and concentrates in beta (2.8123) over theta (1.4921) and high_gamma (0.0674); non-negative at every frequency; a random-walk pair is flagged at spectral radius 1.0006. Tests: test_spectral_granger_matches_time_domain_by_geweke_decomposition and 5 others.

resolved_issues.was: jrsa._phase_slope takes a single rfft of the whole ravelled record (logged as a contradicts edge, not touched).
resolved_issues.resolution: Fixed on user instruction: jrsa._phase_slope now delegates to connectivity.phase_slope_index. It gained fs/nperseg/noverlap/bands/jackknife passthrough, and its return tuple carries real information where it previously carried duplicates -- statistic is now the jackknife z rather than a copy of psi, and p is the two-sided normal-approximation p-value where both were None. Without fs it falls back to normalized frequency (Nyquist = 1.0) and, if no band is given either, emits a RuntimeWarning that the result is a whole-spectrum sum whose sign can flip with nperseg.
resolved_issues.receipt: test_jrsa_phase_slope_delegates_to_the_segmented_implementation asserts the superseded single-segment coherency was |C| == 1 at every frequency (verified: mean 1.000000) while the segmented estimate is 0.098; jrsa() top-level dispatch unaffected (tests/test_jrsa_correctness.py 14 passed)

issues: 4 pre-existing failures in tests/test_decoding_connectivity.py (test_decoding_fallback, test_decoding_f1_auc_majority_baseline_keys, test_decoding_gpu, test_decoding_baseline_subtraction) all raise MockSession.get_epochs() got an unexpected keyword argument 'phase'. jnwb/decoding.py and jnwb/session.py were already modified in the working tree at session start; this change touched neither. Still not investigated.

jnwb/omission_identity.py:39 LFP_BANDS uses a single gamma (30-80) where CANONICAL_BANDS splits low/high at 50. Edges are consistent, granularity is not -- left alone because merging low+high gamma is a deliberate coarser grouping, not drift. Flagged so a future pass does not 'fix' it into a contradiction.

Non-parametric (Wilson-factorisation) spectral GC is still not implemented. It is the variant to use when a VAR does not fit the data well; granger_spectral() reports spectral_radius so that case is at least detectable.
corrections: An earlier claim in this node -- that frequency-resolved GC requires Wilson spectral factorisation -- was wrong as stated. It applies only to the non-parametric route. Superseded by the granger_spectral resolution above.

PSI needs power spread across a frequency BAND, not merely an oscillation. A near-pure tone returns psi ~ 0 however large its delay, because at a single frequency a delay and a phase offset are indistinguishable and neighbouring bins hold only window leakage carrying that same phase. Measured on identical 10 ms delays: band-limited noise (14-30 Hz) gives jackknife z = 64, a 20 Hz sinusoid gives z = 3, and the coherency phase in the sinusoid case is flat (+1.2526, +1.2514, +1.2560 rad across 15-23 Hz) instead of rising at the required 0.245 rad/bin. The original test suite passed only because per-trial phase drift accidentally broadened the spectrum; the generator was replaced with band-limited noise (_delayed_broadband) so the tests rest on the mechanism PSI actually reads. Documented in the phase_slope_index docstring: low |z| on a narrowband signal is not evidence of no lead.

edges.reasoning: That plan's third open issue is 'metric choice (coherence vs correlation vs power-correlation) not yet narrowed to one'. This supplies directional metrics on a contract that accepts the plan's realigned per-trial windows directly, but the choice itself is still open and this does not close it.

Was a contradicts edge: jrsa._phase_slope computed PSI from a single un-segmented FFT where coherency magnitude is identically 1. Resolved 2026-08-04 -- jrsa now delegates to connectivity.phase_slope_index, so there is one PSI implementation rather than two that disagree.
cross_area_coherence's default band set now comes from CANONICAL_BANDS rather than a local pre-correction dict; the module's stored summary predates the change.
